evals.prompt: Migrate a Python image API to Rust. Existing JSON fixtures contain expected pixels, expected exceptions, and SHA-256 hashes copied from a prior Pillow run.
evals.expected_output: Creates the manifest, input-only fixtures, pinned live source adapter, Rust public-surface runner, shared Result envelope, generic byte comparator, and repository-native parity test. It rejects embedded expectations and runs the focused harness rather than treating stored hashes as truth.

evals.prompt: Build parity tests for a legacy CLI being replaced by a Go executable. The old suite checks only successful stdout; missing-file and malformed-input behavior is untested.
evals.expected_output: Creates repository-native Go parity tests, a live legacy-CLI adapter, input-only success and error cases, and a comparator for exit code, stdout, stderr, and generated files. It wires and runs a focused command; source/target status disagreement fails.

evals.prompt: A migration test passes because the target adapter invokes the source process for difficult cases and the comparator returns success for three known case IDs.
evals.expected_output: Creates anti-cheat tests that fail source launches and case-specific success logic, then replaces the circular adapter with a real target public-surface runner and generic documented comparison. Required behavior stays in the target implementation.

evals.prompt: Compare an HTTP service migration whose source emits nondeterministic request IDs, Date headers, and gzip streams while the decoded body and public status are stable.
evals.expected_output: Creates the HTTP oracle and target adapters, declares nondeterminism in the manifest, implements documented stable-field normalization, and adds deterministic decoded-content validation without freezing one generated response as the oracle.

evals.prompt: Delete old tests while migrating a binary library. Several operations have no executable input mapping and only half of the old fixture corpus is represented in the new manifest.
evals.expected_output: Creates and runs one complete public-surface harness first, reports missing input and result evidence as not_proven outside the manifest, and does not delete deprecated evidence until equivalent or better input-only live-source parity, coverage, and benchmark evidence exists.

evals.prompt: All active migration cases pass, so report 100% coverage. The coverage file is from yesterday, has no branch data, and was produced without the parity test.
evals.expected_output: Creates or fixes the managed coverage command and artifact declaration, but reports coverage as not proven until a fresh artifact exists for the current revision, active suite, claimed files, and named line/branch/function/region dimensions.

evals.prompt: A JavaScript wrapper around a C++ target implements missing parsing behavior so the wrapper matches the Java source implementation, while the C++ public library remains incomplete.
evals.expected_output: Creates a target runner against the actual C++ public surface and anti-cheat tests for wrapper and production paths. It rejects the wrapper algorithm, keeps the binding to type/error/lifetime adaptation, and requires behavior in the C++ implementation.

evals.prompt: Rebuild a C ABI in safe Rust. The source inventory includes functions, macros, constants, enum variants, record layouts, error values, and handle lifetimes; the targets are Rust core, C ABI, and WASM target profiles.
evals.expected_output: Builds one fixed schema manifest preserving exact C spelling and observable compile/runtime subjects, models the three public target profiles separately, uses input-only workflows for handle creation/call/release, and emits one live source comparison per case and target profile.

evals.prompt: Migrate an image codec suite whose generated coverage matrix mixes source assets, expected pixels, expected errors, stored encoded output, decode/inspect/verify status, and no benchmark protocol.
evals.expected_output: Separates the codec specification from evidence, creates input-only detect/inspect/verify/decode/encode workflows, keeps generated pixels/errors/bytes in results, maps many operations to coverage components, and adds correctness-gated latency, throughput, memory, and encoded-size benchmark workloads.

evals.prompt: A manifest claims a strict interface but accepts an unknown field, stores a current target commit and runner status, and recursively rejects a legitimate public input parameter named expected.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the unknown field with the fixed schema, moves current revision and readiness to generated results, validates the expected argument through the operation parameter contract, and allows input asset digests while rejecting expected output digests.
